summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent left leg cellulitis, venous insufficiency, and lipodermatosclerosis was admitted due to worsening erythema, pain, and weeping in her left lower extremity despite doxycycline therapy. She was started on IV vancomycin and transitioned to minocycline after consultation with infectious disease. Her infection improved during the hospital stay, and a compression dressing was applied at discharge. She was advised to remove it in three days and follow up with wound care and infectious disease. Iron deficiency anemia was noted, but oral supplementation was poorly tolerated due to chronic pancreatitis; colonoscopy was rescheduled as an outpatient. She remained stable, with pain managed using acetaminophen and oxycodone, and was discharged home with clear instructions on medication changes and wound care.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
